skill.name: 4-step-program
skill.description: Coordinator workflow for AI coding agents that delegates implementation, requires review, verifies issue coverage, and presents PR links.
skill.summary: Run a strict fix, review, iterate, and present loop for AI coding agents.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline examples, placeholder GitHub URLs, and Mermaid diagram text. No prompt injection attempt was found, but the skill intentionally requires GitHub PR review posting, which creates external write side effects that need user authorization.

remediation.issue: Mandatory GitHub review posting can create external write actions.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit confirmation step before creating PRs or posting reviews, and state that review content may leave the local workspace.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI examples may be misread as commands to run automatically.
remediation.suggestion: State that gh commands are illustrative and should run only in the intended repository after user approval.

remediation.issue: The workflow requires PR creation even for tasks that may not need repository artifacts.
remediation.suggestion: Allow non-PR tasks to opt out so agents do not create branches, PRs, or comments for exploratory work.

> When complete, run `Skill(code-reviewer)` on your changes, POST the review to GitHub, and report t
1. Use `Closes #X` or `Fixes #X` in PR body for each issue being addressed
3. Verify issue links with `gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences`
Never write bare `PR #42` or `Issue #100`. **ALWAYS include the full clickable URL.**
**Why this is wrong:** Bare numbers are not clickable. The human must be able to click directly to t
| Bug fix with flow change | `flowchart` showing before/after |
| New API endpoint | `sequenceDiagram` of request flow |
- **Mermaid diagrams** for complex changes (optional but recommended)

**Agents posting reviews to GitHub SHOULD include Mermaid diagrams when helpful.**
4. PRESENT    → Tell human + CONFIRM 100% coverage + LINK the PR URL + Mermaid diagrams (if complex)

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory GitHub Posting Side Effects
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires every code review to be posted to GitHub and mentions mcp__github__create_pull_request_review. This can disclose review content to a repository and create write actions if used without explicit authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple sections make GitHub posting mandatory and name the review creation tool. The risk is clear, but it is part of the declared PR workflow rather than hidden malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Coordinating AI coding agents can leave gaps in issue coverage and reviews. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a strict loop for delegation, review, repair, and PR presentation.
actual_capabilities: Defines a four-step loop for delegating fixes, reviewing work, checking quality, and presenting results.
Requires agents to include all issue requirements in the implementation task.
Requires code-reviewer skill use and GitHub PR review posting.
Adds a final coverage gate with requirement-by-requirement evidence.
Provides anti-pattern examples for incomplete coverage, missing links, and premature approval.
Guides final reports with PR URLs, issue links, and optional Mermaid diagrams.
limitations: Does not implement code by itself; it coordinates other agents and tools.
Assumes a GitHub PR workflow with available issue and pull request access.
May be too strict for exploratory tasks that do not require a PR.
Human review is still needed before merging or deploying changes.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Bug Fixes
use_cases.description: Manage AI-assisted bug fixes while preserving complete issue coverage and visible PR review history.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Reviews
use_cases.description: Require every code change to pass review, correction, and final evidence checks before presentation.

use_cases.title: Build Repeatable Workflows
use_cases.description: Create a consistent delegation pattern for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code coding agents.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Simple Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the 4-step-program to coordinate a bug fix for Issue #[number]. Include all issue requirements, require a PR, and report the PR URL.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Feature Review Loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for a feature request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the 4-step-program to a feature request. Extract every requirement, delegate implementation, require code-reviewer review, and loop until there are zero suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Linked Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate two related issues with the 4-step-program. Link each issue in the PR body, verify closing references, and present coverage evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Manage a Complex Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full 4-step-program for a complex refactor. Use a final requirement table, require GitHub review posting, include diagrams when useful, and escalate after five failed iterations.

output_examples.input: Coordinate an AI agent fixing an authentication bug.
output_examples.output: A delegation summary with every issue requirement, a review gate, a final coverage assessment, and a clickable PR link.

output_examples.input: Check whether an agent can present a feature as complete.
output: Coverage is confirmed for each requirement.
The review is posted to the PR.

output_examples.input: Prepare final status after a reviewed PR.
output_examples.output: A concise human report with completed work, requirement coverage, PR URL, related issue URLs, and remaining risks.

best_practices: Use the skill only when the task should produce reviewed code changes.
Verify issue requirements directly before delegating and before presenting results.
Confirm that GitHub posting is permitted before asking agents to comment on PRs.
anti_patterns: Using the workflow for research-only tasks that do not need a PR.
Accepting a review with suggestions because tests passed.
Posting repository details externally without confirming user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates agents that implement, review, fix, and present code changes.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub?
faq.answer: It is designed for GitHub PR workflows. Other systems need adaptation before use.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written for compatible AI coding tools and agent coordinators.

faq.question: What makes it different from a normal review prompt?
faq.answer: It enforces delegation, posted review, iteration, and a final issue coverage gate.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm repository access, PR policy, and permission to post review comments.

faq.question: What happens if the review is not perfect?
faq.answer: The workflow sends the agent back until issues are fixed or the iteration limit is reached.
